newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: OAU urges states to curb population growth.
newsitem.headline: OAU urges states to curb population growth.

text.p: The Organisation of African Unity appealed to member states on Monday to take measures against continental population growth expected to reach 1.6 billion by the year 2025.

"Unless appropriate and timely solutions are identified and implemented, the African continent will find itself teeming with 1.6 billion people who would mostly be underfed, malnourished and diseased," Vijay Makha, assistant OAU secretary-general, told an African Population Commission conference.
Makha urged states to link measures to improve life expectancy with improved social systems, addressing not only economic growth but food security, health, education and employment.
"As much as population is an asset for a nation, it can easily constitute a negative factor to sustainable development when allowed to grow faster than the economy", he said.
Africa's economic growth rate stands at around 2.9 percent annually. Current population is around 750 million.

The four-day Commission, organised by the OAU, the Economic Commission for Africa and the African Development Bank, will draw up strategies for population and development in Africa beyond this century, conference organisers said.
